our_title: graphLoad accepts negative vertex labels, used unchecked as indices in graphLoad2
ran: cd $WORK/repro && ./runall.sh pristine: `gtst GRA-04/neglbl.grf` -> 'AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 ... #0 _SCOTCHgraphLoad2 graph_io.c:305' (64-bit: rejected by luck as 'graphLoad2: duplicate vertex label'); series 32/64 -> 'graphLoad: bad input (3)'. Fuzz (1500 mutants, seed 1234): bucket graphLoad2 remains on pristine; on the series the label bound also removes 'graph_io.c:298 signed integer overflow 2147483647 + 1' (PS2-G14-1).
severity_note: Agree high: user-supplied .grf, out-of-bounds heap read at a file-controlled offset in a public API (SCOTCH_graphLoad).
evidence: graph_io.c:194 `if (intLoad (stream, &vlblval) != 1) {      /* Read label data */` (no sign check); :305 `if (indxtab[vlbltax[vertnum]] != ~0) {`.
review_accuracy: Accurate for 7.0.16. In 7.0.17 the edge-end half is fixed; the label half is not. Review's suggested fix (reject labels <0 and >vlblmax at read) is right for the lower bound; an upper bound at read is impossible since vlblmax grows while reading, but is unnecessary because graphLoad2 allocates indxtab to vlblmax+1 and bounds edge ends by it.
first_pass_critique: Correct status (partially-fixed) and correct preferred fix. Its note that large labels allocate a huge indxtab is right and is a real residual (see extra PS2-G14-1: vlblmax+1 overflow / huge alloc). It missed the distributed and mesh twins (dgraphLoadCent/Dist, meshLoad) which have the same unchecked label read.

extra_instances.quote: if (intLoad (stream, &vlblval) != 1) { ... meshptr->vlbltax[vertnum] = vlblval + vertbas + baseadj;  then graphLoad2 called at :294

fix_options.label: Reject negative labels and range-check edge ends at read time (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Add (vlblval < 0) to the label read; for unlabeled graphs range-check each base-adjusted edge end against [baseval,vertnnd[.
fix_options.tested: Built 32-bit and 64-bit ASan+UBSan (0 warnings); neglbl.grf and badend.grf/conv.grf now rejected; m4x4/base-0/base-1/labelled g.grf still load; check_prog_gbase/gmk/gout/gpart, check_scotch_graph_dump/map/order/induce/coarsen pass.
fix_options.tradeoffs: One comparison per vertex/arc; rejects only invalid files. No ABI change.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Mirrors febaef7's own in-loop reject style (graph_io.c:236,246) and graphLoad's existing header checks (graph_io.c:131-139).

fix_options.label: Range-check inside graphLoad2
fix_options.summary: Reject vlbltax[vertnum] < 0 before using it as an index in graphLoad2.
fix_options.tested: untested: alternative not built; preferred option was built and tested. Would stop the OOB read but leaves GRA-10 (unlabeled edge ends) unguarded and adds a branch to the relabeling loop. [7.0.18: diff no longer applies]
fix_options.tradeoffs: Protects all graphLoad2 callers in one place; does not cover the unlabeled edge-end path.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Less likely: the maintainer validates untrusted values where they are read (febaef7), not deep in a shared relabeling helper.

notes: 7.0.17 status: partially-fixed -> 7.0.18 status: partially-fixed (febaef7's negative edge-end check only; labels unchanged). 45a4de85 (snprintf of proptab) and 9c51d9df touch graphLoad but not labels. intLoad (ff9d5a54, reviewed by G07: correct) now rejects values beyond INTVALMAX, which does not affect our '!= 1' tests. Patch rebased by hand (now 0005), with labels >= GNUMMAX also rejected.

our_title: Matrix Market loader overflows the vertex array for base other than 1
ran: ./runall.sh pristine: `gcv -im0 t0b.mtx /dev/null` -> 'AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4 ... _SCOTCHgraphGeomLoadMmkt graph_io_mmkt.c:229'; `gcv -im2 t2c.mtx` then gtst -> 'graphLoad: invalid arc count (1)'; series 32/64 -> both load and gtst passes.
severity_note: Agree medium: converter (gcv) over a user .mtx; one-past heap write for base 0, wrong result for base 2.
evidence: 7.0.17: 'while (vertnum < mrownbr) grafptr->verttax[++ vertnum] = edgenum;' then 'grafptr->verttax[++ vertnum] = edgenum;' - vertnum is based, mrownbr is unbased.
review_accuracy: Accurate, including the fix (loop to vertnnd-1). graphCheck is only the base-2 symptom; the real defect is the unfilled trailing entries.
first_pass_critique: Correct status and preferred fix (loop to vertnnd-1).

fix_options.label: Compare in based space (recommended)
fix_options.tested: Built 32/64-bit (0 warnings); -im0/-im1/-im2 load and pass gtst; gcv chac/mtx round-trips of m4x4/m4x4_b1/small1/p2-p2 clean under ASan.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Two-token change, no effect for base 1, no ABI change.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Uses the structure's own based bound (vertnnd); idiomatic throughout the tree.

fix_options.label: Normalise indices to base 0 while reading
fix_options.summary: Work in unbased space, add baseval only at the writers.
fix_options.tested: untested: structural alternative not implemented in full. [7.0.18: diff no longer applies]
fix_options.tradeoffs: Cleaner model but rewrites much of a rarely used converter; larger regression risk.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Unlikely for a bugfix release; too invasive versus the two-token fix.

notes: 7.0.17 status: still-present -> 7.0.18 status: still-present. Patch rebased unchanged (now 0001).

our_title: Chaco loader edge-array bound off by one and checked after the store
ran: ./runall.sh pristine: `gcv -ic over.chac /dev/null` -> 'heap-buffer-overflow WRITE ... _SCOTCHgraphGeomLoadChac graph_io_chac.c:230' (64-bit pristine: 'bad input (5)' by luck); series 32/64 -> 'graphGeomLoadChac: bad input (5)'. Fuzz: pristine-32 bucket graphGeomLoadChac gone on the series.
severity_note: Agree medium: converter over a user .chac; heap write past the based edge array.
evidence: 7.0.17: 'if (edgenum > (grafptr->edgenbr + 1))' (chac:225) runs AFTER 'grafptr->edgetax[edgenum ++] = chavertnum;' (chac:230) and edlotax is stored even earlier; the bound is one too permissive for a base-1 array.
review_accuracy: Accurate; review's 'edgenum >= edgenbr + baseval' equals edgenbr+1 since Chaco base is 1.
first_pass_critique: Correct; preferred hoist-and-tighten matches what I committed.

fix_options.label: Hoist and tighten the check (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Test edgenum >= edgenbr+1 before reading/storing any arc data.
fix_options.tested: Built 32/64-bit (0 warnings); over.chac rejected, valid chac loads, gcv round-trips clean.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Rejects over-long adjacency earlier; same error number kept.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Bound-before-store is the pattern used by the HB loader and graphLoad.

fix_options.label: Guard the edlotax store only
fix_options.summary: Keep the late check but add the bound into the edlotax read condition.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Smaller diff but leaves read/check order convoluted.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Less clean; he prefers an explicit guard before the store.

notes: 7.0.17 status: still-present -> 7.0.18 status: still-present. Patch rebased onto his 'return (1);' style commit (now 0006).

our_title: Scotch geometry loader keeps the dimension in a local; saved geometry empty
severity_note: Agree medium: silent wrong result through a public API (SCOTCH_graphGeomLoadScot/geomData/SaveScot); no crash.
evidence: dimnnbr is a local (scot:90); geomptr->dimnnbr is never assigned in graphGeomLoadScot; geomtab is allocated only when NULL, ignoring a stored dimension.
review_accuracy: Accurate, including the geomtab-reuse size hazard.
first_pass_critique: Correct; its preferred memRealloc approach is what I used, but I reallocate unconditionally (handles a changed vertnbr at the same dimension too, not just a changed dimension).

extra_instances.quote: Gnum dimnnbr; ... (geomptr->geomtab == NULL) && memAlloc(...); geomptr->dimnnbr never set - identical bug in the mesh twin (G11's file)

fix_options.label: (Re)allocate geomtab and record the dimension (recommended)
fix_options.summary: memRealloc geomtab to vertnbr*dimnnbr and set geomptr->dimnnbr.
fix_options.tested: Built 32/64-bit (0 warnings); gra09 reports dim=2 and saves all coordinates; no leak (memRealloc reuses the existing block).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Reallocates every call (negligible); assumes geomtab came from memAlloc, which holds for geomInit users.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: memRealloc(NULL,...) idiom is used across the tree; fixes both the missing dimension and the stale-size reuse in one place.

fix_options.label: Record the dimension only; refuse a differing reuse
fix_options.summary: Set dimnnbr, keep the conditional alloc, error if an existing geomtab has another dimension.
fix_options.tested: untested: alternative not built. [7.0.18: diff no longer applies]
fix_options.tradeoffs: Smallest change, never reallocs caller memory, but cannot reuse a Geom across dimensions.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Acceptable but less flexible than reallocating.

notes: 7.0.17 status: still-present -> 7.0.18 status: still-present. Patch rebased unchanged (now 0003). With it, PS2-G11-mesh-struct-io-7 (base mismatch for unlabeled graphs) becomes visible: saved geometry of a base-1 graph cannot be reloaded.

evidence: 7.0.17 stores 'grafptr->edgetax[edgenum] = edgeval + baseadj;' (graph_io.c:251) with only edgeval<0 checked at read; no upper bound and no base-adjusted lower bound.

our_title: Harwell-Boeing loader: row check off by one, column pointers unchecked
ran: Kit rebuilt this round ($WORK/repro/GRA-11/*.hb, 4x4 PSA pattern). Pristine 7.0.18: bad99.hb and bad0.hb -> 'graphGeomLoadHabo: bad input (9)' (fixed by 0ef275a0); badn1.hb (row 5 = n+1) -> loads (rc 0), hbpart harness -> 'graphCheck: invalid edge numbers'; baddec.hb (column pointers 1 5 3 7 8) -> loads and passes graphCheck with arcs silently dropped; badcol.hb (pointer 99) -> 'bad input (8)' only because the file ends. Series 32/64: badn1 -> 'bad input (9)', badcol/baddec -> 'bad input (10)', ok.hb loads.
severity_note: Agree medium: converter over a user .rsa; OOB vertex-array access from a file-controlled row index (0 or >order).
location_7_0_18: src/libscotch/graph_io_habo.c:276 (row check), 216-242 (column pointers, only the last one checked at 243)
evidence: graph_io_habo.c:276 `if (habnzrval < grafptr->baseval || habnzrval > grafptr->vertnnd) {` (vertnnd = vertnbr + 1 is one past the last vertex); :241 `habcoltab[habcolnum] = habcolval;` with no check of intermediate values.
upstream_change: 0ef275a0 Add sanity check to Harwell-Boeing graph format loader [report R. Perry]

upstream_fix_review.details: Right: row indices are now range-checked unconditionally after decoding, and the error paths are factored through one fail: label (graph_io_habo.c:236-240, inside the EOF test block). Wrong bound: '> grafptr->vertnnd' accepts vertnnd (n+1), one past the last vertex; such a file loads and produces a graph that fails graphCheck ('invalid edge numbers'). Style: missing parentheses around the two comparisons. Missing: intermediate column pointers are not checked (a decreasing pointer silently drops non-zeros; a large one drives habnzrnum past habnzrtab), field values and format numbers still accumulate in a signed int (UBSan at :270, :392, :425; EOF spin with huge widths). The mesh twin meshGeomLoadHabo (G11) got nothing.
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Ours (7.0.17 0004) used '(habnzrval < 1) || (habnzrval > habcolnbr)', which is exact. His fail: factoring is nicer and kept. Rebased as 0007 (bound fixed to '>= vertnnd' + column pointer checks), plus 0008 (header sizes) and 0009 (format widths, EOF, saturated decoding).

review_accuracy: Accurate; the loader additionally trusts the column-pointer array habcoltab (see extra PS2-G14-1).
first_pass_critique: Correct. First pass bundled GRA-11 with GRA-24 in one diff; I split them into two commits (distinct logical defects: a range check vs a parser typo).

extra_instances.quote: ELTPTR/VARIND range checks exist only under SCOTCH_DEBUG_MESH2 - same class, tracked by review id SEP-08 (G11)

our_title: graphCheck does not enforce vertex-label uniqueness
ran: ./runall.sh pristine: `tl 1` -> 'graphCheck=0' (duplicates accepted); series 32/64 -> 'ERROR: graphCheck: duplicate vertex label' 'graphCheck=1'; `tl 0` -> graphCheck=0 on both.
severity_note: Low: reachable only by building a graph with duplicate labels via SCOTCH_graphBuild; file loaders already reject duplicates. Impact is a silent wrong mapping, not corruption.
evidence: graphCheck never reads grafptr->vlbltax; yet graphLoad2 (graph_io.c:304), graphGeomLoadScot (graph_io_scot.c:162) and SCOTCH_graphTabLoad (library_graph_map_io.c:137) all treat duplicate labels as an error, and doc s_f.tex states labels must be unique.
review_accuracy: New defect (not in the review); related to API-21 (graphTabLoad reads one element past mappsorttab).
first_pass_critique: First pass reproduced it and preferred rejecting in graphCheck; I agree and implemented that, since uniqueness is a documented Graph invariant that only graphCheck can catch for a built (not loaded) graph.

fix_options.label: Reject duplicates in graphCheck (recommended)
fix_options.summary: When vlbltax != NULL, sort a copy of the labels and reject equal neighbours.
fix_options.tested: Built 32/64-bit (0 warnings); tl 1 rejected, tl 0 accepted; check_scotch_graph_map/order/induce/coarsen and check_prog_gtst/gbase/gmk/gout/gpart (all on labelled graphs) still pass.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Adds an O(V log V) sort and a memAlloc to a Check routine that was allocation-free, so the check can now fail with out-of-memory. Internal graphs never carry duplicate labels, so no legitimate graph is rejected.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Section 3.3 of the maintainer guide: a Check method verifies internal consistency; label uniqueness is such an invariant, enforced everywhere else at construction. DECISION FOR MAINTAINER: whether allocation inside graphCheck is acceptable; alt-B avoids it.

fix_options.label: Leave graphCheck; harden consumers
fix_options.summary: Keep Check allocation-free and make label consumers robust (e.g. graphTabLoad / API-21).
fix_options.tested: untested: alternative not built. [7.0.18: diff no longer applies]
fix_options.tradeoffs: No allocation in Check, but whack-a-mole across every label consumer and never surfaces the invalid graph to the user.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He may prefer this if he wants graphCheck to stay allocation-free; otherwise the invariant check is cleaner.

notes: 7.0.17 status: still-present -> 7.0.18 status: still-present. Patch rebased unchanged (now 0004); design choice for the maintainer as in 7.0.17.

our_title: Graph loaders trust header counts, label values and HB field widths
ran: $WORK/repro/PS2-G14-1: pristine 32-bit `gtst maxlbl.grf` -> 'graph_io.c:298:27: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 2147483647 + 1'; `gcv -im negmm.mtx` / `gcv -ic negchac.chac` -> negative sizes reach memAlloc ('requested allocation size 0xfffffffffffffff8' under ASan); fuzz pristine-32: TIMEOUT (chac, rsa), graphGeomLoadHaboFormat and graphGeomLoadHabo signed overflows, memAllocGroup. Series: 'graphLoad: bad input (3)', 'graphGeomLoadMmkt: invalid matrix size', 'graphGeomLoadChac: invalid graph size'; fuzz series-32: 1 bucket left (edge load sum overflow, see notes).
evidence: Chaco: 'grafptr->vertnbr = chavertnbr; grafptr->edgenbr = chaedgenbr * 2;' with no sign/range check. Mmkt: 'memAlloc (2 * linenbr * sizeof ...)' with linenbr unchecked. graph_io.c:297 'memAlloc ((vlblmax + 1) * sizeof (Gnum))' where vlblmax can reach GNUMMAX. HB format: 'number = number * 10 + *charptr - '0';' with no width bound, used as a getc loop count.

extra_instances.quote: edlosum += grafptr->edlotax[edgenum] = (Gnum) edloval;  (sum of user edge loads overflows; same for velosum)
habcolnbr = (Gnum) atol (&habmatbuf[2][29]);  (long truncated to a 32-bit Gnum before our range check)

fix_options.label: Header size checks + HB width/EOF/saturation + label bound
fix_options.summary: 0008 (Chaco/MM/HB header counts), 0009 (HB format numbers <= 80, EOF-bounded fields, saturated decoding), 0005 (labels < GNUMMAX), 0007 (HB column pointers).
fix_options.tested: PS2-G14-1 files and fuzz (pristine-32 9 buckets/133 hits -> series-32 1/3; pristine-64 6/53 -> series-64 3/34, all three ASan 'out of memory' on file-declared sizes of 16-300 GB).

our_title: graphLoad accepts negative degrees; 9c51d9df overflow test relies on signed wraparound
ran: $WORK/repro/PS2-G14-2: pristine 32/64 `gtst negdeg.grf` (degree -1 after a degree-2 vertex) -> graphLoad succeeds, only gtst's graphCheck fails ('arc data do not match'); pristine 32 `gtst hugedeg.grf` -> 'graph_io.c:224:13: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 2 + 2147483647' then 'invalid arc count (1)'. Series 32/64: 'graphLoad: bad input (5)' and 'invalid arc count (1)' with no UBSan report. Fuzz: pristine bucket graphLoad (iter 60, same overflow) gone on the series.
evidence: graph_io.c:224-226 `degrval += edgenum; if ((degrval > edgennd) || (degrval < 0)) {` -- the addition overflows before the test; :215 `if (intLoad (stream, &degrval) != 1) {` accepts negative degrees.
upstream_change: 9c51d9df Add edge count overflow check to graph loading [report Z. Li]

upstream_fix_review.details: It rejects a negative running arc count after 'degrval += edgenum'. That addition is itself the overflow (signed, undefined behavior; UBSan reports it on hugedeg.grf); the test works only because GCC wraps in practice. A negative degree is still accepted whenever the running count stays non-negative (negdeg.grf loads; the arcs of the vertex silently disappear and graphLoad returns success). Twins: dgraph_io_load.c degree reads and meshLoad (G11 0010) not touched.
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Ours rejects degrval < 0 at read time and tests 'degrval > (edgennd - edgenum)' before adding, which is overflow-free; his commit is subsumed. Rebased 0005 replaces his test by ours.

fix_options.label: Reject negative degree and test overflow before adding
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Small change in the lines he just touched.

notes: 7.0.17 status: still-present -> 7.0.18 status: partially-fixed (9c51d9df catches overflowing degrees through wraparound only, accepts negative degrees).
